variants.headline: Looking back: party divides in two
variants.sub: The colony has seen a party divide into two organisations.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A political party had split in two in {colony}.

Political unity has value when it enables common convictions to act. It is not a principle that can settle every disagreement by itself. Our movement should judge a division by the commitments at stake, rather than granting either unity or separation an automatic claim to righteousness in every case.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We judge {target} harshly in this matter. Political organisation carries obligations beyond the comfort of its leaders, and division is an appropriate occasion to question the quality of that stewardship.

variants.headline: Looking back: a political organisation breaks apart
variants.sub: A split has divided a political party in the colony.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The colony had seen a party divide into two organisations.

Political unity has value when it enables common convictions to act. It is not a principle that can settle every disagreement by itself. Our movement should judge a division by the commitments at stake, rather than granting either unity or separation an automatic claim to righteousness in every case.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.
